design_rationale: The study is a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, multicentre trial where pregnant women were randomly assigned (1:1) using a computer-generated random allocation sequence.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated, concealed via a central web-based system managed by a third party, and baseline characteristics between the two arms were well-balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomisation was performed by a computer-generated random allocation sequence in variable blocks of two, four and six. Randomisation was stratified by trial site, plurality and gestational age (<28 weeks and ≥ 28 weeks). The randomisation process was carried out by a third party (DEFACTUM, Central Region Denmark). When oral and written consent had been obtained from the eligible women, the attending obstetrician accessed a web-based program (Trialpartner) with a centre-specific log-on procedure.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants, carers, and trial personnel were blinded with identical-appearing infusion bags, deviations were minimal, and an intention-to-treat analysis was performed.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The infusion bags containing MgSO4 and placebo were identical in appearance. The participants, caregivers, and study coordinators at all sites, as well as the investigators were blinded to treatment assignment until all data were collected, the data analyses completed, and the tables and figures were made... The primary data analysis was performed for all enrolled patients on an intention-to-treat basis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were complete for 100% of the randomised fetuses and children via nationwide medical records review and mortality tracking.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 321 (100%) were followed-up through medical records... 313 (100%) were followed-up through medical records... 343 Foetuses and children included in the primary analysis... 337 Foetuses and children included in the primary analysis

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors and investigators were blinded to allocation, and standardized, validated criteria (GMFCS and ASQ) were used to ascertain cerebral palsy.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was moderate to severe CP defined as a Gross Motor Function Classification System (GMFCS) of level II to V... The participants, caregivers, and study coordinators at all sites, as well as the investigators were blinded to treatment assignment until all data were collected, the data analyses completed, and the tables and figures were made.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered with a pre-specified analysis plan, and reported results reflect the pre-specified outcomes and intention-to-treat analysis without selective outcome reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The planned statistical analyses were described before being carried out.21 The primary data analysis was performed for all enrolled patients on an intention-to-treat basis... Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01492608.

overall_summary: The study is a rigorously conducted double-blind, placebo-controlled randomised trial with centralized computer-generated randomization, full blinding of participants and assessors, virtually complete follow-up of all participants, and pre-specified intention-to-treat analyses, resulting in low risk of bias across all domains.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned to magnesium sulphate or saline placebo using a computer-generated randomisation schedule with central telephone allocation.
overall_summary: The study was well-conducted with robust central randomisation, blinded outcome assessment, and nearly complete follow-up, but raises some concerns in Domain 2 due to an open-label/single-blind design where treating clinicians were unblinded to assignment.

design_rationale: The study is a multicenter, double-blind randomized clinical trial in which pregnant individuals were randomly assigned to intravenous magnesium sulfate or placebo via a central telephone randomization service.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence was randomly generated with variable block sizes, concealed via central telephone randomization, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Eligible pregnant individuals were randomly assigned to the magnesium group or the placebo group using a central telephone randomization service... The randomization schedule used balanced, variable block sizes and was performed by an investigator not involved in clinical care. There was stratification by hospital site, gestational age (30-31 weeks' gestation and 32-33 weeks' gestation), and the number of fetuses (1 or 2).

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blinded with identical placebos, protocol adherence was very high (~95%), and analyses followed an intention-to-treat approach.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A study number was allocated at randomization that corresponded to a treatment pack containing either magnesium sulfate or placebo (an isotonic sodium chloride solution). Participants, staff, investigators, and assessors of the children were blinded to the treatment allocation... Almost 95% of participants in each group received the allocated treatment... conducted following a prespecified statistical analysis plan with an intention-to-treat approach

domain_judgments.rationale: Although ~19% of surviving children lacked in-person pediatric assessment for the primary complete-case analysis, missingness was balanced across groups and a prespecified sensitivity analysis incorporating 96% of children yielded consistent results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the infants alive at trial entry, 691 of 858 (80.5%) in the magnesium group and 674 of 821 (82.1%) in the placebo group were included for the primary outcome of death or cerebral palsy (determined by pediatric assessment) at 2 years. The sensitivity analysis, which incorporated data from all sources (pediatrician, psychometrist, caregiver questionnaires, and caregiver), included 823 children (95.9%) in the magnesium group and 785 children (95.6%) in the placebo group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Standardized and objective diagnostic criteria were applied by blinded pediatricians and assessors across both trial groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants, staff, investigators, and assessors of the children were blinded to the treatment allocation... Surviving children were assessed by a pediatrician and an assessor trained to administer the third edition of the Bayley Scales of Infant Development (BSID-III) as close as possible to 2 years' corrected age.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, protocol and statistical analysis plans were published in advance, and reported primary and secondary outcomes correspond with prespecified analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The unadjusted and adjusted analyses for hospital site, gestational age at entry, and number of fetuses were conducted following a prespecified statistical analysis plan with an intention-to-treat approach... A prespecified sensitivity analysis examined the primary outcome using information from all data sources

overall_summary: The study is a rigorously conducted multicenter double-blind randomized clinical trial with concealed central allocation, low risk of confounding or deviations, standardized blinded outcome measurement, robust sensitivity analyses for missing data, and adherence to a prespecified analysis plan. All RoB 2 domains were assessed as low risk of bias.

design_rationale: The trial is explicitly described as a randomized controlled trial in which participants were randomly assigned to magnesium sulfate or placebo using computer-generated randomization numbers with masked treatment packs.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated, centrally managed, and concealed using sequentially numbered, masked treatment packs, with baseline characteristics balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study randomization numbers were generated by computer with variable block sizes of 4, 6, or 8 and managed by nonclinical staff at the University of Adelaide's Maternal Perinatal Clinical Trials Unit. Each study number was placed on a masked treatment pack. Packs were sent to participating centers ready for use. Eligible women who gave written informed consent were enrolled by taking the next treatment pack, corresponding to the number of fetuses, from the drug supplies held at the center.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and perinatal staff were blinded to treatment allocation using identical treatment packs, protocol deviations were minimal and balanced, and analysis adhered to the intention-to-treat principle.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Each treatment pack looked identical and contained an infusion bag of 60 mL of either a 0.5-g/mL solution of magnesium sulfate or isotonic sodium chloride solution (0.9%)... All perinatal staff were blinded to treatment group allocation... All statistical analyses were undertaken on an intention-to-treat basis, including outcome data from women who did not give birth preterm.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for 99% of surviving children at 2-year follow-up, with very few losses to follow-up that are unlikely to introduce meaningful bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Outcome data were obtained, up to the time of hospital discharge, on all 1062 women and their 1255 infants alive at the time of randomization, and 2-year corrected age outcomes were available for 1047 children (99% of 2-year survivors). Fourteen children (9 in the magnesium sulfate group and 5 in the placebo group) without 2-year corrected age cerebral palsy assessments were treated as missing data and excluded from the cerebral palsy analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary outcomes of mortality and cerebral palsy were assessed using standard definitions by assessors and an independent committee blinded to treatment assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All pediatric deaths were reviewed by an independent committee, blinded to therapy, to determine the principal cause of death. Surviving children were assessed at a corrected age of 2 years by developmental pediatricians and psychologists blinded to treatment group allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes, analyses, and primary endpoints were pre-specified in the protocol and reported fully and consistently according to the planned intention-to-treat approach.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcomes were total pediatric mortality up to a corrected age of 2 years (including stillbirths, neonatal deaths, and mortality after hospital discharge), cerebral palsy at a corrected age of 2 years, and the combined adverse outcome of death or cerebral palsy at 2-year follow-up.

overall_summary: This randomized controlled trial had rigorous methodology across all domains, including computer-generated masked allocation, successful double-blinding, 99% follow-up of surviving infants at 2 years, blinded outcome assessment, and complete reporting of pre-specified outcomes. Consequently, the overall risk of bias is low.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned using a computerized program with stratified block randomization.

domain_judgments.rationale: A computerized stratified block randomization program was used, allocation sequence generation was robust, and baseline characteristics were balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: To ensure balance in the randomization process, a computerized program that had been written by Information Medical Services, Bethesda, Md, under contract to the National Institute for Neurological Disorders and Stroke, National Institutes of Health, Bethesda, Md, was used. Consenting women were randomized in stratified blocks of 6 on the basis of race (black versus other) and gestational age (≤28 weeks vs >28 weeks).

domain_judgments.rationale: The tocolytic arm was open-label with tocolytic choice left to attending obstetrician discretion, raising potential concerns for co-intervention deviations, although intention-to-treat analyses were conducted.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In the tocolytic arms, the women were randomized to treatment with either (1) MgSO4 given as a 4-g bolus followed by an infusion of 2 to 3 g of MgSO4 per hour or (2) other tocolytic therapy, according to the attending obstetrician's choice among ritodrine, terbutaline, indomethacin, or nifedipine. In the doubly masked 'preventive' arms, women were randomized to receive either (1) a 4-g intravenous bolus of MgSO4 only, without further MgSO4 infusion or (2) saline solution control.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary composite clinical trial outcome data were available for all 165 randomized infants without notable attrition, although secondary biomarker analyses were restricted to a subset with available cord blood.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The 149 trial participants gave birth to 165 infants (133 singletons and 16 pairs of twins)... Of 165 infants in the study, 37 infants (22%) had adverse health outcomes, as defined (neonatal IVH, PVL, cerebral palsy, or death)... Of 165 infants, 82 infants have both umbilical cord serum ionized magnesium levels and health outcome data available for analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors (pediatric radiologists and developmental pediatrician) were blinded to antenatal treatment group allocation, and objective standardized definitions were used.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Final ultrasound diagnoses, including grading of intracranial hemorrhage, when present, were made by consensus decisions of 2 pediatric radiologists... The developmentalist was masked to the antenatal exposure variables.

domain_judgments.rationale: No pre-trial registration or protocol is cited to confirm that the composite outcome definitions, post-hoc cutoffs (e.g., dichotomizing ionized magnesium at 0.60 mmol/L), and multivariable model specifications were prespecified.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Regarding the composite adverse outcome variable (neonatal IVH + PVL + total pediatric death + cerebral palsy), we performed 2 separate analyses. The first analysis was by intention to treat, as modeled in the ORACLE trials. The second was an evaluation of the composite adverse outcome variable as it related to the umbilical cord serum ionized magnesium level at delivery.

overall_summary: The trial utilized computerized stratified block randomization and blinded outcome assessment, but has some concerns regarding open-label intervention in the tocolytic trial and potential selection in reported analyses and post-hoc biomarker cutoffs without a prospective protocol.

design_rationale: The study is a multicenter, double-blind randomized controlled trial using a computer-generated random allocation sequence.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants were allocated using a computer-generated random sequence stratified by clinical center and gestational age with matching placebo, and baseline characteristics were balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Group assignment was made according to a computer-generated random sequence, with stratification according to clinical center and, in twin pregnancies, weeks of gestation (<28 or ≥28).

domain_judgments.rationale: The study used an identical-appearing placebo with blinding of participants and trial personnel, and an intention-to-treat approach was used for the analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Eligible, consenting women were randomly assigned in a double-blind fashion to receive either intravenous magnesium sulfate (a loading dose of 6 g infused for 20 to 30 minutes, followed by a maintenance infusion of 2 g per hour) or identical-appearing placebo. ... The data from all patients were analyzed according to the group to which they were randomly assigned, regardless of whether they received the study medication.

domain_judgments.rationale: Follow-up was achieved for 95.6% of children, with low and balanced rates of missing data between groups that are unlikely to introduce substantial bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was assessed for 95.6% of fetuses. ... The baseline characteristics of the women whose fetuses were lost to follow-up did not differ significantly between the two study groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors were certified pediatricians or pediatric neurologists blinded to intervention assignment, using standardized and validated assessment criteria.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: An annually certified pediatrician or pediatric neurologist made a diagnosis of cerebral palsy if two or more of the following three features were present... For 28 children who were not evaluated at 2 years of age but were not declared free of cerebral palsy at the age of 1 year, two pediatric neurologists who were unaware of the treatment assignment judged whether the children had moderate or severe cerebral palsy on the basis of a review of the 1-year examination.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial had a registered protocol (NCT00014989), prespecified primary and secondary outcomes, and reported all prespecified analyses accordingly.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was the composite of stillbirth or infant death by 1 year of corrected age or moderate or severe cerebral palsy at or beyond 2 years of corrected age. ... (ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT00014989.)

overall_summary: The study is a well-designed, placebo-controlled, double-blind randomized clinical trial with adequate sequence generation and concealment, high follow-up rate, blinded outcome assessment, and complete reporting according to a prespecified protocol. All five RoB 2 domains were assessed as low risk of bias.
